The three-banded flag tetra (Hyphessobrycon heterorhabdus) was scientifically described in 1894; the animals on which the description was based came from the Brazilian state of Pará, and more detailed information or illustrations are not available.

From 1910 and in the 1920s, when tetras became the most popular aquarium fishes, three-banded tetras also came to Europe. These animals had a red, a white and a black longitudinal band over the entire body length, hence the name three-banded tetras. According to some sources they came from the lower Rio Tocantins (whose lower reaches are in Pará), according to other sources from the southern tributaries of the middle Amazon (i.e. Rio Madeira, Rio Tapajós, Rio Xingu).

A whole group of species has been named after the three-banded tetra, the Hyphessobrycon heterorhabdus group. They share a black longitudinal band as a common characteristic. Many new species from this group have been described in recent years and some more are known but not yet formally described, which makes identification difficult.

Animals of this group have now been received with the locality Apeú. It is not specified whether this means the district of the large city Castanhal in Pará or the small river Apeú, which flows through the district of the same name. Freshly arrived, the animals showed only two stripes, one light and one black, so the species was first determined as Hyphessobrycon agulha, but after a few days of acclimation red coloured scales also became visible above the light longitudinal band. The opinion is that this is indeed the "true" H. heterorhabdus, while the central Amazonian form mentioned in the old literature probably belonged to the species Hyphessobrycon sateremawe, described only in 2020. H. sateremawe differs from H. heterorhabdus by a much wider black longitudinal band.
